name: Candidate Database Breach
description: An intrusion exposes the candidate database — resumes, Social Security numbers, background-check results, and salary histories for hundreds of thousands of applicants.
assumptions: Record count spans years of retained applications, not just active candidates.
Primary loss covers forensics, notification, and credit monitoring at scale.
Secondary loss covers client contract losses and state AG enforcement.

name: Contractor Payroll Diversion
description: Attackers phish contractor portal credentials or spoof HR to change direct-deposit details, diverting weekly payroll across many placed workers.
assumptions: Weekly pay cycles cap the diverted amount per event; the agency makes workers whole.
High placement volume makes lures routine; attempts track workforce size.
Secondary loss covers client-site friction and worker attrition after incidents.

name: Client Portal Account Takeover
description: Credential attacks take over client hiring-manager accounts in the ATS portal, exposing requisitions, rates, and candidate files across accounts.
asset: Applicant tracking system and client portal
assumptions: A campaign counts when it takes over at least one client account with data access.
Primary loss covers investigation, resets, and per-client disclosure.
Secondary loss covers contract penalties under client data-protection addenda.

name: Ransomware Disrupts Placement Operations
description: Ransomware encrypts the ATS, payroll, and onboarding systems in the middle of the placement week; recruiters work from spreadsheets and phones.
assumptions: Missing a payroll run is the loss driver; emergency manual payroll is assumed to work.
Backups restore core systems within three business days.
Secondary loss covers client defections to competing agencies mid-engagement.

name: Departing Recruiter Takes the Book
description: A departing recruiter exports client contacts, requisitions, rates, and candidate pipelines to launch a competing desk.
asset: Client relationships and candidate pipeline data
assumptions: Frequency tracks recruiter turnover; vulnerability reflects export monitoring and offboarding speed.
Primary loss is margin on placements moved within the first year.
Secondary loss covers enforcement litigation against non-solicit breaches.
